members.summary: Frozen configuration for every MobileNet-v4 variant.
members.extended:
One dataclass describes the whole family; `variant` selects which of
the paper's five searched architectures (Appendix D, Tables 11-15) is
built, and the remaining fields cover the classifier and regularisation
knobs that are not part of the searched topology.

parameters.name: num_classes
parameters.description: Output classes of the classification head.

parameters.name: in_channels
parameters.description: Channels of the input image.

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description:
Which searched architecture to build — one of `"conv_small"`,
`"conv_medium"`, `"conv_large"`, `"hybrid_medium"` or
`"hybrid_large"`.  The variant fixes the block sequence, the
stem width (24 for the Large models, 32 otherwise), the activation
(GELU for Hybrid-Large, ReLU for the rest) and whether residual
branches carry a layer scale (hybrids only).

parameters.name: dropout
drop_path_rate
parameters.description:
Peak stochastic-depth rate.  Block `i` of `n` drops its
residual branch with probability `drop_path_rate * i / n`.  The
paper's recipe peaks at 0 (Conv-Small), 0.075 (Medium) and 0.35
(Large) during training (Table 10); the default leaves it off so
the model behaves deterministically unless a recipe asks for it.

raises.description:
If `variant` is not one of the five paper variants, or a rate
lies outside $[0, 1)$.

examples:
>>> from lucid.models.vision.mobilenet_v4 import MobileNetV4Config
>>> cfg = MobileNetV4Config()
>>> cfg.model_type
'mobilenet_v4'
>>> cfg.variant, cfg.num_classes
('conv_small', 1000)
>>> MobileNetV4Config(variant="hybrid_large").variant
'hybrid_large'
notes:
Block sequences follow the authors' released implementation, which is
what the published checkpoints were trained against.  The four other
variants match Tables 11, 12, 14 and 15 block for block.  For
Hybrid-Medium the released model orders several UIB blocks differently
from Table 13 and carries one extra block in the stride-32 stage; its
parameter count (10.56 M in units of $2^{20}$) is the 10.5 M
that Table 6 reports.

members.name: MobileNetV4
members.extended:
Implements the searched architectures of Qin et al., "MobileNetV4:
Universal Models for the Mobile Ecosystem", ECCV 2024
([arXiv:2404.10518](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10518)).  The trunk is a stride-2 stem followed by five
stages built from the **Universal Inverted Bottleneck** (UIB), whose
two optional depthwise convolutions let the architecture search pick
an inverted bottleneck, a ConvNeXt-like block, an FFN or the new
ExtraDW block at every position; a fused inverted bottleneck opens the
medium and large models, and the hybrid variants interleave **Mobile
MQA** attention blocks into the two deepest stages.  The last stage is
a $1 \times 1$ convolution widening the stride-32 map to 960
channels.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
Architecture spec.  Use the factory functions
(`mobilenet_v4_conv_small`, `mobilenet_v4_conv_medium`,
`mobilenet_v4_conv_large`, `mobilenet_v4_hybrid_medium`,
`mobilenet_v4_hybrid_large`) for the paper's variants.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.vision.mobilenet_v4 import mobilenet_v4_conv_small
>>> backbone = mobilenet_v4_conv_small().eval()
>>> out = backbone(lucid.randn(1, 3, 224, 224))
>>> out.last_hidden_state.shape
(1, 960, 7, 7)
>>> [f.reduction for f in backbone.feature_info]
[4, 8, 16, 32]
notes:
The UIB computes



$$
y = x + \gamma \odot
    P\bigl(D_{\mathrm{mid}}(E(D_{\mathrm{start}}(x)))\bigr),
$$

with $E$ the pointwise expansion (norm + activation), $P$
the linear pointwise projection, each $D$ an optional depthwise
convolution and $\gamma$ a per-channel layer scale present only
in the hybrid variants.  The residual is used whenever the block keeps
both resolution and width.

attributes.name: config
attributes.description: The config that built this model.

attributes.name: act
attributes.description: Stem activation (ReLU, or GELU for Hybrid-Large).

attributes.name: blocks
attributes.description:
Five stage `Sequential` containers; stage $i$ ends at stride
$2^{i+2}$ for $i \le 3$, and stage 4 is the 960-channel
$1 \times 1$ widening layer.

attributes.name: feature_info
attributes.description:
One entry per output resolution (strides 4, 8, 16 and 32); the
stride-32 entry reports the 960 channels that
`forward_features` returns.

members.name: MobileNetV4ForImageClassification

methods.name: forward
methods.signature: forward(x: Tensor, labels: Tensor | None = None)

members.summary: MobileNet-v4 image classifier with the post-pool head.
members.extended:
Runs the `MobileNetV4` trunk and the head of the paper's tables:
the 960-channel map is globally average-pooled *first*, then widened by
a $1 \times 1$ convolution to 1280 channels with normalisation
and activation, and finally projected to the classes,

$$
\operatorname{AvgPool} \to \operatorname{Conv}_{1\times1}^{1280}
    \to \operatorname{BN} \to \sigma \to \operatorname{Dropout}
    \to \operatorname{Linear}.
$$

Pooling before the widest layer is the MobileNet-v3 head redesign; the
normalisation after that layer is new in v4.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
Architecture spec.  Use the `*_cls` factories
(`mobilenet_v4_conv_small_cls` and siblings) for the paper's
variants.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.vision.mobilenet_v4 import mobilenet_v4_conv_small_cls
>>> model = mobilenet_v4_conv_small_cls().eval()
>>> out = model(lucid.randn(2, 3, 224, 224))
>>> out.logits.shape
(2, 1000)
Retarget the head for a 10-class task:
>>> model = mobilenet_v4_conv_small_cls(num_classes=10).eval()
>>> model(lucid.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)).logits.shape
(1, 10)
notes:
When `labels` are passed to `forward`, the categorical
cross-entropy against the logits is returned as `loss`.

attributes.name: config
attributes.description: The config that built this model.

attributes.name: conv_stem, bn1, act, blocks
attributes.description:
The same trunk as `MobileNetV4`, held directly on the
classifier so the parameter names match the released checkpoints.

members.name: mobilenet_v4_conv_large
members.extended:
Builds a `MobileNetV4` with the Conv-Large architecture of
Qin et al., 2024 (Appendix D, Table 14): a 24-channel stem, a fused-IB stage, and two deep stages of ExtraDW and ConvNeXt-like blocks up to 512 channels, closed by a
$1 \times 1$ widening to 960 channels.  30.08 M
parameters without the classification head.

parameters.name: pretrained
parameters.description:
Must stay `False` — no checkpoint is published for the headless
backbone, and `True` raises rather than returning random
weights.  The ImageNet-1k checkpoint belongs to the matching
`*_cls` classifier, whose error message this names.

parameters.name: **overrides
parameters.description:
Keyword overrides merged into `MobileNetV4Config`
(e.g. `drop_path_rate=0.1`).

returns.description: Backbone returning the stride-32, 960-channel feature map.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.vision.mobilenet_v4 import mobilenet_v4_conv_large
>>> model = mobilenet_v4_conv_large().eval()
>>> model(lucid.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)).last_hidden_state.shape
(1, 960, 7, 7)
notes:
Qin et al., "MobileNetV4: Universal Models for the Mobile Ecosystem",
ECCV 2024 ([arXiv:2404.10518](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10518)).  The paper trains and evaluates this
variant at 384x384; the network is fully convolutional up to the
pool, so any input whose sides are multiples of 32 works.

members.name: mobilenet_v4_conv_large_cls
members.signature: mobilenet_v4_conv_large_cls(pretrained: bool | str = False, weights: MobileNetV4ConvLargeWeights | None = None, overrides: object = {})
members.extended:
Builds a `MobileNetV4ForImageClassification` with the Conv-Large
architecture (Qin et al., 2024, Appendix D, Table 14) and the
post-pool head (960 → 1280 → classes).  32.59 M parameters;
Table 6 reports 82.9% ImageNet-1k top-1 at 31 M parameters and
5.9 G MACs.  Classifier dropout defaults to the paper's 0.2
(Table 10).

parameters.name: pretrained
parameters.description:
Pretrained-weight selector.  `False` → random init; `True` → the
`DEFAULT` tag
(`MobileNetV4ConvLargeWeights.E600_R384_IN1K`); a tag string
(e.g. `"E600_R384_IN1K"`) → that specific checkpoint. Mutually
exclusive with `weights` (which wins if both are given).

parameters.name: weights
parameters.description:
Explicit weights enum member, e.g.
`MobileNetV4ConvLargeWeights.E600_R384_IN1K`.  Takes precedence
over `pretrained`.

parameters.name: **overrides
parameters.description:
Keyword overrides merged into `MobileNetV4Config`
(typically `num_classes` to retarget the head).  Overriding
`num_classes` away from the checkpoint's 1000 makes pretrained
loading fail the strict key/shape check — load with the
matching head, then call `reset_classifier`.

returns.description:
Classifier with the Conv-Large configuration (plus `overrides`),
optionally initialised from pretrained weights.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.vision.mobilenet_v4 import mobilenet_v4_conv_large_cls
>>> model = mobilenet_v4_conv_large_cls(num_classes=10).eval()
>>> model(lucid.randn(2, 3, 224, 224)).logits.shape
(2, 10)
Load ImageNet-pretrained weights:
>>> model = mobilenet_v4_conv_large_cls(pretrained=True)
>>> from lucid.models.weights import MobileNetV4ConvLargeWeights
>>> model = mobilenet_v4_conv_large_cls(
...     weights=MobileNetV4ConvLargeWeights.E600_R384_IN1K
... )
notes:
Qin et al., "MobileNetV4: Universal Models for the Mobile Ecosystem",
ECCV 2024 ([arXiv:2404.10518](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10518)).  Parameter names match timm's
implementation, so its ImageNet-1k checkpoints load with an identity
key map.  The paper evaluates this variant at 384x384.

Pretrained weights are converted from timm's
`mobilenetv4_conv_large.e600_r384_in1k` — timm's own ImageNet-1k
training of this architecture, trained at 384x384; the authors released
none — and hosted on the Hugging Face Hub under
`lucid-dl/mobilenet-v4-conv-large`.  timm reports 82.974% top-1 /
96.244% top-5 for it at 384x384 with the preset that
`MobileNetV4ConvLargeWeights.E600_R384_IN1K.transforms` reproduces
(384 crop, 404 resize, bicubic, ImageNet mean/std).

members.name: mobilenet_v4_hybrid_medium_cls
members.signature: mobilenet_v4_hybrid_medium_cls(pretrained: bool | str = False, weights: MobileNetV4HybridMediumWeights | None = None, overrides: object = {})
members.extended:
Builds a `MobileNetV4ForImageClassification` with the Hybrid-Medium
architecture (Qin et al., 2024, Appendix D, Table 13) and the
post-pool head (960 → 1280 → classes).  11.07 M parameters;
Table 6 reports 80.7% ImageNet-1k top-1 at 10.5 M parameters and
1.2 G MACs.  Classifier dropout defaults to the paper's 0.2
(Table 10).

parameters.name: pretrained
parameters.description:
Pretrained-weight selector.  `False` → random init; `True` → the
`DEFAULT` tag
(`MobileNetV4HybridMediumWeights.IX_E550_R256_IN1K`); a tag
string (e.g. `"IX_E550_R256_IN1K"`) → that specific checkpoint.
Mutually exclusive with `weights` (which wins if both are given).

parameters.name: weights
parameters.description:
Explicit weights enum member, e.g.
`MobileNetV4HybridMediumWeights.IX_E550_R256_IN1K`.  Takes
precedence over `pretrained`.

parameters.name: **overrides
parameters.description:
Keyword overrides merged into `MobileNetV4Config`
(typically `num_classes` to retarget the head).  Overriding
`num_classes` away from the checkpoint's 1000 makes pretrained
loading fail the strict key/shape check — load with the
matching head, then call `reset_classifier`.

returns.description:
Classifier with the Hybrid-Medium configuration (plus `overrides`),
optionally initialised from pretrained weights.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.vision.mobilenet_v4 import mobilenet_v4_hybrid_medium_cls
>>> model = mobilenet_v4_hybrid_medium_cls(num_classes=10).eval()
>>> model(lucid.randn(2, 3, 224, 224)).logits.shape
(2, 10)
Load ImageNet-pretrained weights:
>>> model = mobilenet_v4_hybrid_medium_cls(pretrained=True)
>>> from lucid.models.weights import MobileNetV4HybridMediumWeights
>>> model = mobilenet_v4_hybrid_medium_cls(
...     weights=MobileNetV4HybridMediumWeights.IX_E550_R256_IN1K
... )
notes:
Qin et al., "MobileNetV4: Universal Models for the Mobile Ecosystem",
ECCV 2024 ([arXiv:2404.10518](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10518)).  Parameter names match timm's
implementation, so its ImageNet-1k checkpoints load with an identity
key map.  The paper evaluates this variant at 256x256.

Pretrained weights are converted from timm's
`mobilenetv4_hybrid_medium.ix_e550_r256_in1k` — timm's own ImageNet-1k
training of this architecture, trained at 256x256; the authors released
none — and hosted on the Hugging Face Hub under
`lucid-dl/mobilenet-v4-hybrid-medium`.  timm reports 81.478% top-1 /
95.692% top-5 for it at 256x256 with the preset that
`MobileNetV4HybridMediumWeights.IX_E550_R256_IN1K.transforms`
reproduces (256 crop, 269 resize, bicubic, ImageNet mean/std).

summary: MobileNet v4 family — Qin et al., 2024.
citation: Qin, Danfeng, et al. "MobileNetV4: Universal Models for the Mobile Ecosystem." Computer Vision – ECCV 2024, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 15098, Springer, 2024.
theory:
MobileNet-v4 is built around a single searchable block, the
**Universal Inverted Bottleneck** (UIB).  It extends the inverted
bottleneck of MobileNet-v2 with two *optional* depthwise convolutions:
one before the $1 \times 1$ expansion and one between the
expansion and the $1 \times 1$ projection,



$$
\mathrm{UIB}(x) = x + \gamma \odot
    P\bigl(D_{\mathrm{mid}}(E(D_{\mathrm{start}}(x)))\bigr),
$$

where $E$ is the pointwise expansion, $P$ the linear
pointwise projection, and each $D$ is either a depthwise
convolution or the identity.  The four on/off combinations recover four
familiar blocks: the classic inverted bottleneck (**IB**, middle
depthwise only), a **ConvNeXt-like** block (start depthwise only, a
cheap large-kernel spatial mix before the expansion), a transformer
**FFN** (neither — two pointwise layers), and the new **ExtraDW**
block (both), which deepens the network and widens its receptive field
at almost no cost.  Because the expansion and projection are shared by
all four instantiations, a NAS super-network over UIB shares more than
95% of its parameters, and the search simply decides which depthwise
layers to keep at each position.  The stems use a *fused* inverted
bottleneck — a dense $3 \times 3$ convolution into a
$1 \times 1$ projection — which is faster than a depthwise pair
at high resolution.

The hybrid variants interleave UIB blocks with **Mobile MQA**, a
multi-query attention block tuned for accelerators: every query head
shares a single key and value head, which raises operational intensity
when the token count is small relative to the channel width, and the
keys and values can be spatially reduced by a stride-2
$3 \times 3$ depthwise convolution,



$$
\mathrm{MQA}(X) = \mathrm{Concat}_{j=1}^{h}\!\left[
    \mathrm{softmax}\!\left(
        \frac{(X W^{Q}_{j})\,(\mathrm{SR}(X) W^{K})^{\top}}
             {\sqrt{d_k}}\right)
    \mathrm{SR}(X) W^{V}\right] W^{O}.
$$

Sharing keys and values cuts attention latency by more than 39% on
mobile accelerators relative to multi-head attention at a negligible
accuracy cost.  Residual branches of the hybrids are scaled by a
learnable per-channel layer scale $\gamma$ initialised at
$10^{-5}$.

Five models come out of the search: **Conv-Small**, **Conv-Medium**
and **Conv-Large**, built only from UIB and fused-IB blocks, and
**Hybrid-Medium** and **Hybrid-Large**, which add Mobile MQA to the
last two stages.  Every model ends with the MobileNet-v3 style head
that moves the widest $1 \times 1$ layer after global pooling.
They are mostly Pareto-optimal across mobile CPUs, DSPs, GPUs, the
Apple Neural Engine and the Pixel EdgeTPU at once, ranging from 73.8%
ImageNet-1k top-1 at 0.2 GMACs (Conv-Small) to 83.4% (Hybrid-Large).
